# What is local marketing? Strategies that actually work

Learn tested local marketing techniques to reach, persuade, and convert your ideal customers.

[

![](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fartisanai-storage.sfo3.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com%2Fblog-authors%2Fsam-rinko.png&w=96&q=75)

Sam Rinko](https://www.artisan.co/authors/sam-rinko)11 minutes read·Jul 18, 2025

![What is local marketing? Strategies that actually work](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fimages.ctfassets.net%2Fkyprwggh4muz%2F01EsJ71vrDkp2DSbRwBZyN%2F700eed820628a9e78daddcc5f1f510db%2FWhat_Is_Local_Marketing__Cover_.webp&w=1200&q=75)

Most articles on the internet preach marketing tactics that only work for companies with a global audience. 

Local business owners are left asking, “How do we find customers who live nearby?”

Today, you’ll learn the seven local marketing strategies—from local SEO to geo-targeted ads—that skilled business owners use to generate high-quality local leads.

## What Is Local Marketing?

Local marketing targets leads in a specific geographic area, often near the physical storefront of a business. 

To attract and convert local prospects, businesses host community events, run local advertising campaigns, optimize their website for local SEO, and leverage other localized traditional and digital marketing techniques. 

Local marketing is most common among these types of businesses:

*   **Local brick-and-mortar businesses with a physical presence**, like restaurants, gyms, mechanics, and bookstores. 
    
*   **Service providers** such as plumbers, realtors, or lawyers, who offer services to businesses and individuals in a specific location.
    
*   **Franchises and chains** like a Subway or a grocery store targeting local communities. 
    

Whether you’re a small business owner or a marketer at an enterprise brand, [local lead generation](https://www.artisan.co/blog/local-lead-generation) enables you to spend your money and time on high-quality leads who will actually visit your store or use your service.

According to [research by SOCi](https://www.soci.ai/insights/nurturing-the-customer-relationship-top-takeaways-from-socis-2024-consumer-behavior-index/), 80% of US consumers search for local businesses weekly. If you don’t show up when prospects make these searches, you’ll lose out on potential custom. 

By boosting your presence on social media sites, search engine results pages, and Google Maps, a local marketing strategy helps your business get on—and stay on—the radar of nearby leads. 

## Targeting the Right Local Audience

![Targeting the Right Local Audience](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fimages.ctfassets.net%2Fkyprwggh4muz%2F4ZNvujWPcM5iYLTU4WV1C8%2F5b80901a4ebfe025294449206ae7e505%2FTargeting_the_Right_Local_Audience.webp&w=3840&q=75)

To identify the right local audience, create an [ideal customer profile (ICP)](https://www.artisan.co/blog/targeted-lead-generation). This is a description of your target customers that takes into account their demographics, pain points, and behaviors. 

Here’s how to create an ICP: 

1.  **Use an** [**ICP template**](https://offers.hubspot.com/ideal-customer-profile-icp) **to get started:** A template tells you which questions to ask your customers.
    
2.  **Run customer surveys and interviews**: Gather information about your happiest customers. 
    
3.  **Look for patterns in their responses:** Are a lot of them parents? Do they mostly come from one wealthier neighborhood? Do they share similar reasons for visiting? List all shared attributes. 
    

Once you have the first version of your ICP, which you’ll revise as you learn more about your customers, you’re ready to **start reaching out to them.** 

![Automate your outbound with an AI BDR](/_next/image?url=%2Fassets%2Fstartups%2Fava-web.webp&w=750&q=75&dpl=dpl_4F8Dx7E3GtLr1MERK7PbWRp5EZUv)

### Automate your outbound with an AI BDR

Meet Ava—your AI BDR who handles prospecting, outreach, and follow-ups, so your team can focus on closing.

Book a demo

## Local Marketing Strategies That Work

![7 Local Marketing Strategies That Work](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fimages.ctfassets.net%2Fkyprwggh4muz%2F62zv89ZLoSoNxOIgHo9vws%2F28aee702a1bba77305004f69aacfc21b%2F7_local_marketing_strategies_that_work.webp&w=3840&q=75)

### 1\. Use Social Media to Reach Locals

Whether you’re running local ads on Instagram or posting pictures of happy customers on LinkedIn, social media marketing is a fantastic way to generate local leads. 

In fact, according to SOCi, 73% of consumers discover new brands on social media.

Here are the best ways to generate [local leads](https://www.artisan.co/blog/ai-lead-nurturing) through social media: 

*   **Run geo-targeted social ads:** Leverage social platforms’ local targeting features to run ads to people in specific zip codes, cities, and neighborhoods. 
    
*   **Engage in local online groups or pages:** Post in community forums and on social pages to build trust with community members. For example, a childcare service owner in Norwell might join and start posting tips in the “MOMS Club of Norwell” Facebook group.
    

![MOMS Club of Norwell](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fimages.ctfassets.net%2Fkyprwggh4muz%2F3PWanjTWnntTX6cU7617ws%2F2d46c1e74ae4ee4d23463e5636874d3a%2FMOMS_Club_of_Norwell.png&w=3840&q=75)

*   **Post location-specific content and hashtags:** Use local hashtags to ensure posts appear in potential customers’ social feeds. And tie your message to local events and challenges that matter to people who live here. For example, a fencing company in Minnesota might post about snow-resilient outdoor paint. 
    
*   **Collaborate with local influencers:** Tap into someone else’s large local following. For example, a new Thai restaurant might direct message a local food influencer on YouTube and ask them to review their restaurant in return for a free meal. 
    

Your marketing doesn’t have to be super flashy to win new business. The important thing is to put yourself out there. Use social media to tell locals what you do and who you help, with photo evidence of your successes and testimonials, if you have them. 

If anyone in that town ever needs a shed, there’s a good chance they’ll think of him. Notice the “Coach” tactically thrown into the post. That’s a trust builder. People love to work with someone who is involved in a town in ways other than just selling to its residents, which brings us nicely to our next tip.

People buy from those they like and trust. And what better way to inspire those feelings about your business than a good conversation with customers?

## How local SEO becomes a serious growth channel for your business

Local SEO is often underestimated. Create a Google Business Profile, collect some reviews, and done. But the businesses that get real results know it's more involved. The power of local visibility lies in the connection between your website and Google Maps. Strong local landing pages boost your listings. And strong listings drive traffic to your pages.  

Yet we often hear: "There isn't much volume in local SEO." That makes sense if you're working with just one listing for one address. But once you start scaling the system, the game changes. Multiple locations, virtual expansions, listings at strategic addresses. Suddenly, local SEO becomes a scalable channel.  

"Most agencies optimize either your Google Business Profile or your website. The real wins come from connecting the two."

We've rolled this out internationally for clients like Autolift. A combination of optimized Google Maps listings and local landing pages that reinforce each other. The same principle works for Brugman Letselschade and The Phone Lab: systematically building local presence, even in locations without a physical office.  

The result? More local leads, more store visits, better rankings in the local pack. And above all: a channel that keeps performing without constantly throwing media budget at it.  

That's what our SEO team excels at. Building local visibility that lasts.
